gaps.sentence: Her memoir ___ (translate) into fourteen languages so far.
gaps.explanation: 'So far' requires present perfect passive: has been + translated (singular 'memoir').
'By + future time' signals future perfect passive: will have been + processed.

gaps.sentence: My laptop ___ (service) next week, so back up your files beforehand.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' takes the future passive: will be + serviced (is being serviced is also a valid arrangement).

gaps.sentence: By next June, the entire collection ___ (move) to the new wing.
gaps.explanation: Future perfect passive: will have been + past participle for something finished by 'next June'.

gaps.sentence: The castle ___ (restore) at present, so the east wing is closed to visitors.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + restored for work in progress now.

gaps.sentence: All the passwords ___ (reset) after last week's security breach.
gaps.hint: recent past, plural subject, present relevance
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: have been + reset for a recently completed action.

gaps.sentence: The decision ___ (announce) at yesterday's press conference.
gaps.explanation: 'Yesterday' signals past simple passive: was + announced.

gaps.sentence: The refugees ___ (provide) with blankets and hot meals last night.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: were + provided. Note the pattern provide somebody WITH something.
